headline: Dhanmondi: Journalist injured in attack by Jamaat activists
summary: Mahfuzur Rahman Shishir of the daily Sokal was allegedly punched and kicked after a dispute broke out during a party procession.
details: A journalist was injured after being assaulted allegedly by activists of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami during an altercation between reporters and party activists at Dhanmondi 32 in Dhaka this morning.
The injured journalist was identified as Mahfuzur Rahman Shishir, a reporter for the daily Sokal.
Jamaat-e-Islami's Dhanmondi Zone had organized a procession to prevent possible sabotage ahead of the 77th founding anniversary of the Awami League, whose activities remain banned.
Witnesses said a dispute broke out between Jamaat activists and journalists during a briefing after the procession. It could not be immediately known what triggered the altercation.
Some Jamaat activists allegedly accused a journalist of being an Awami League supporter. When reporters protested, the argument turned violent.
Activists allegedly grabbed Shishir by the collar and punched him. As he fell to the ground, some of them kicked him, according to witnesses.
Fellow journalists rescued him and took him to a nearby private hospital for treatment.
Shishir criticized the attack, questioning how such violence against journalists represents the freedom of the press.

Abdus Sattar Sumon, assistant secretary for publicity affairs of Jamaat-e-Islami's Dhaka South city unit, called the incident 'unfortunate' and stated they do not support misconduct towards journalists.
The party said they will identify those involved through footage and take organizational action against them, while also investigating if outsiders were involved.

Shishir criticized the attack, questioning how such violence against journalists represents the freedom of the press.

Abdus Sattar Sumon, assistant secretary for publicity affairs of Jamaat-e-Islami's Dhaka South city unit, called the incident 'unfortunate' and stated they do not support misconduct towards journalists.

headline_marked: 26 [[Awami League leaders arrested]] in Dhaka drives
headline: 26 Awami League leaders arrested in Dhaka drives
summary: Dhaka Metropolitan Police conducted separate operations across the capital to arrest members of the banned party and its associate bodies.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested 26 leaders and activists of the Awami League and its associate bodies in separate drives across the capital yesterday.
According to a press release signed by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Media) Niaz Mehdi, the arrests took place in several areas including Dhanmondi, Mohammadpur, Ramna, and Khilkhet.
Specifically, ten people were arrested from Dhanmondi, eight from Mohammadpur, and two each from Ramna and Khilkhet.
One person each was arrested from the Banshal, Kadamtali, Mirpur, and Turag police station areas.
Police stated that these operations are intended to maintain public safety and normal law and order in the capital.
Legal proceedings against the individuals arrested are currently underway.
